rationale: The base station is online locally (live view works, siren works, cloud time sync ok) but event reports repeatedly fail with E-503 "TLS handshake error", so events never reach the cloud and no push notifications are delivered. Router/base restart did not clear the error, and the TLS handshake failure pattern matches the historical case of an expired device certificate on the backend, which requires FAE escalation.

output.symptom_summary: Customer reports no push notifications on phones since last week, despite siren working locally. Base station online, live view works on local Wi-Fi, but event reports fail with E-503 TLS handshake error.
output.suspected_root_cause: Expired device certificate on backend causing TLS handshake failure for cloud event reporting.
key_abnormal_indicators: Error code E-503 (cloud report failed: TLS handshake error) persists after router and base station restart
Base station online locally (uplink_status: ok, live view works, siren works)

results.text: Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

Uplink loss of the base station, pairing timeouts, capacity limit reached, weak signal of a single device, low battery, outdated peripheral firmware that upgrades successfully via OTA, and full storage. Provide the customer with step-by-step instructions and confirm the issue is resolved.
